newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't coffee auction expected July 9 - union.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't coffee auction expected July 9 - union.

text.p: A Brazilian government coffee auction, scheduled to be held on July 2, is now expected to take place on July 9 due to a change in auction rules, said the president of the Sao Paulo Coffee Industry Union.
The change involves an extension in payment terms to 120 days from 60 days, approved last week by the country's National Monetary Council.

However the change must first be published in the country's official gazette and then Banco do Brasil, responsible for holding the electronic auctions, must give five working days' notice of the quantities and qualities of coffee involved in the sale, Nathan Herszkowicz said.
Although no quantity has so far been set, the sale is likely to be for around 300,000 60-kg bags, he added.
A Banco do Brasil official said the bank had received no information from the Industry and Commerce Ministry over when the next auction would take place.
David Nahum, secretary general of the Brazilian Coffee Industry Association (ABIC), said that he expected the next sale to take place between July 10-15.
The delay should only affect the July sale, officials said.
Other auctions during 1997/98 (July/June) are scheduled as follows, according to ABIC.
